newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VICTORIOUS PEARCE PUTS LEAGUE SURVIVAL FIRST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICTORIOUS PEARCE PUTS LEAGUE SURVIVAL FIRST.

text.p: Two goals in five minutes by Ian Woan enabled Nottingham Forest to come from behind and beat Newcastle 2-1 in the English F.A. Cup fourth round on Sunday.
After a tense first half stalemate, England striker Les Ferdinand headed home a John Beresford cross in the 60th minute to the delight of the home fans.

Forest, currently battling to climb out of the premier league relegation zone, fought back and equalised in the 76th minute when a long range shot by Woan, who had failed to score previously this season, was deflected past Newcastle keeper Shaka Hislop by Beresford.
Four minutes later Beresford miskicked a clearance and Woan pounced to hammer the ball into the top corner from 25 metres.
It was Forest's fifth successive victory under player-manager Stuart Pearce.
But Pearce was reluctant to claim any credit for the turnaround in the club's fortunes and stressed that premier league survival was his priority.
"I don't think it's just down to self-belief. That takes away a bit of what (previous manager) Frank Clark's done at the club," said Pearce.
"I thought he was desperately unlucky not to turn results around."
And while Forest fans eagerly awaited Sunday evening's fifth round draw, Pearce said he was "not that fussy about the cup".
"To be honest, avoiding relegation in my only target this season."
